## Premise corrections first

Two names in your question don't exist in this tree (Linux 7.0, `028ef9c96e96`):

- **`i915_pm_runtime_suspend`** — no such symbol. The runtime-PM suspend callback is **`intel_runtime_suspend`** (`i915_driver.c:1545`), installed as `i915_pm_ops.runtime_suspend` (`i915_driver.c:1752`).
- **`intel_display_suspend`** — no such symbol. The equivalent is **`intel_display_driver_suspend`** (`display/intel_display_driver.c:684`), called from `i915_drm_suspend` at `i915_driver.c:1120`.

`rg -n "i915_pm_runtime_suspend|intel_display_suspend" drivers/gpu/drm/` returns nothing.

## Call chains reaching `i915_pm_suspend`

`i915_pm_suspend` (`i915_driver.c:1392`) is itself a PM callback, not something called from other callbacks. It is referenced exactly twice, both as function pointers in `const struct dev_pm_ops i915_pm_ops` (`i915_driver.c:1718`):

```
i915_pm_ops.suspend   = i915_pm_suspend   (i915_driver.c:1719)   <- PMSG_SUSPEND (S0ix/S3)
i915_pm_ops.poweroff  = i915_pm_suspend   (i915_driver.c:1745)   <- PMSG_HIBERNATE (S4)
```

So the only "callers" are the PM core dispatching through `dev_pm_ops`. Downstream:

```
[PM core] .suspend / .poweroff
  └─ i915_pm_suspend(kdev)                        i915_driver.c:1392
       ├─ kdev_to_i915(kdev)                      i915_drv.h:328
       ├─ guard: drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF -> return 0
       └─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)            i915_driver.c:1103
```

`i915_drm_suspend` has three call sites (no others reach it):

| Caller | Site | Entry point |
|---|---|---|
| `i915_pm_suspend` | `i915_driver.c:1404` | `.suspend`, `.poweroff` |
| `i915_pm_freeze` | `i915_driver.c:1493` | `.freeze` (S4 image creation) |
| `i915_driver_suspend_switcheroo` | `i915_driver.c:1223` | vga_switcheroo, via `i915_switcheroo.c:42` (not a PCI PM callback) |

The sibling PCI PM callbacks that do **not** reach `i915_pm_suspend`/`i915_drm_suspend`: `i915_pm_prepare`, `i915_pm_suspend_late`, `i915_pm_suspend_noirq`, `i915_pm_poweroff_late`, `i915_pm_poweroff_noirq`, `i915_pm_freeze_late` (these go to `i915_drm_suspend_late`/`i915_drm_suspend_noirq`, `i915_driver.c:1150`+).

## Which of those callers also call the runtime-suspend path

**None.** `intel_runtime_suspend` is referenced only once outside its definition — as the `.runtime_suspend` pointer at `i915_driver.c:1752`. There is no call edge from `i915_pm_suspend`, `i915_pm_freeze`, or `i915_driver_suspend_switcheroo` into it. The system-suspend and runtime-suspend paths are strictly parallel entry points from the PM core; they only converge on shared leaf helpers, e.g. both call `intel_uncore_suspend()` / `intel_pxp_*suspend()` / `intel_display_power_*` variants, and they interlock through `disable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(&dev_priv->runtime_pm)` on the same `dev_priv->runtime_pm`.

## Data flow of `dev_priv` from `i915_drm_suspend` to `intel_display_driver_suspend`

```c
/* i915_driver.c:1392 */
i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
    struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);   /* dev_get_drvdata(kdev), i915_drv.h:328 */
    i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm);                         /* passed as struct drm_device * */

/* i915_driver.c:1103 */
i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
    struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);     /* container_of back to dev_priv */
    struct intel_display *display   = dev_priv->display;  /* i915_drv.h:172, line 1106 */
    ...
    intel_display_driver_suspend(display);                /* line 1120 — only `display` crosses */

/* display/intel_display_driver.c:684 */
intel_display_driver_suspend(struct intel_display *display)
    drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm);              /* back to drm_device via display->drm */
    display->restore.modeset_state = state;
    flush_workqueue(display->wq.cleanup);
    intel_dp_mst_suspend(display);
```

Key point: `dev_priv` is **not** propagated into the display layer. The pointer chain is
`kdev → (drvdata) → dev_priv → &dev_priv->drm → (to_i915) → dev_priv → dev_priv->display → display->drm`.
`intel_display_driver_suspend` sees only the opaque `struct intel_display *`, which re-derives the `drm_device` via `display->drm` — this is the deliberate i915↔display decoupling, so the display code never touches `drm_i915_private`.

Other `dev_priv` uses inside `i915_drm_suspend` that stay in the i915 layer: `intel_irq_suspend(dev_priv)` (1122), `to_gt(dev_priv)->ggtt` (1132), `suspend_to_idle(dev_priv)` (1136), `dev_priv->suspend_count++` (1139), `i915_gem_drain_freed_objects(dev_priv)` (1145), and `&dev_priv->runtime_pm` for the wakeref assert bracket (1109/1143).
